newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU hopes Stet soon to compensate Omnitel.
newsitem.headline: EU hopes Stet soon to compensate Omnitel.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday he was optimistic Italian state telecommunications holding company Stet would soon pay 60 billion lire ($35.5 million) to Omnitel to compensate for the fee it paid to become the country's second mobile phone operator.
"(Stet) management told me that this was now going to happen," Van Miert said referring to a meeting last week with the new management.
The European Commission has been at pains to ensure fair competition in Italy's expanding mobile phone market.

Omnitel, a consortium in which Olivetti is the largest shareholder, had to pay 750 billion lire in 1995 in return for an operating licence. Italy's first mobile operator TIM, which is controlled by Stet, did not have to pay a licence fee.
But despite an agreement between the EU and Italian government at the end of 1995, Omnitel complained earlier this month that the agreed compensation had not been paid yet.
